issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class defines a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but the Stock class (in the template) calls getQuantity(). This name/signature mismatch causes a compilation error and prevents students from running or implementing the intended behavior. The problem statement also instructs students to add getters for private fields, and the solution uses getQuantity(), so the template is inconsistent with both the usage and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template StockIngredient API consistent with its usage and the solution: rename the retrieveQuantity() method to getQuantity(), or add a public getQuantity() that returns the same value (delegating to retrieveQuantity()). Ensure Stock.java calls match the getter name (getQuantity) used throughout the problem and solution.

issues.description: The template defines a StockIngredient quantity accessor named retrieveQuantity(), while the Stock implementation (and the solution and problem statement) use the conventional getter name getQuantity(). This naming mismatch prevents a clear mapping between the problem description and the template code and causes compile/runtime mismatches when Stock calls getQuantity().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java (template), or add a getQuantity() method that returns the same value (delegating to retrieveQuantity()). This will align the template with the problem statement and solution and avoid compilation/mapping confusion.
